draft.title: Oxidation and reduction
card: the loss of electrons by an atom, ion or molecule. For example, Zn becomes Zn²⁺ and loses 2 electrons.
the gain of electrons by an atom, ion or molecule. For example, Cu²⁺ becomes Cu and gains 2 electrons.
Electrons do not stay free in a reaction. If one species loses electrons, another species gains them, so oxidation and reduction always happen together.
A reaction with both is a redox reaction. In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, zinc is oxidised and copper(II) ions are reduced.
draft.remember: Oxidation is loss of electrons, reduction is gain, and one cannot happen without the other.

a.q: In the reaction Mg + Fe²⁺ → Mg²⁺ + Fe, what happens to the magnesium?
opts: It is oxidised because it loses electrons
It is reduced because it loses electrons
It is oxidised because it gains electrons
It is reduced because it gains electrons
a.why: Mg becomes Mg²⁺, so each atom loses 2 electrons. Losing electrons is oxidation. Reduction is the opposite process, and here it happens to the iron ions.
a.clue: Compare the charge on magnesium before and after.

b.q: Mia places a copper wire in silver nitrate solution and silver metal forms on it: Cu + 2Ag⁺ → Cu²⁺ + 2Ag. Which statement is correct?
opts: Silver ions gain electrons while copper loses electrons
Silver ions lose electrons while copper gains electrons
Silver ions are oxidised and copper is reduced
Copper is reduced and no species is oxidised
b.why: Ag⁺ becomes Ag, so silver ions gain electrons and are reduced. The electrons come from copper, which becomes Cu²⁺ and is oxidised. Reduction cannot occur alone, so some species must be oxidised.
b.clue: Check which species changes to a lower charge, and where its electrons came from.

a.best: It is oxidised because it loses electrons

b.best: Silver ions gain electrons while copper loses electrons
